title: Decision Exposure Buckets: cost-prioritized sampling and enriched snapshots for fallback routing analysis
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Improve the signal available for investigating region selection, tier routing decisions, and fallback model variant activations by introducing 'Decision Exposure Buckets' — a cost-aware sampling mechanism that captures enriched per-decision snapshots (compact traces + per-hop micro-metrics + model variant diffs) while bounding egress/storage cost. This ticket implements the sampling policy, snapshot schema, ingestion pipeline, and dashboard queries needed for SRE/Platform/Support to triage routing degradations and fallback regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A cost-aware sampler exists that buckets requests into exposure levels (none, low, medium, high) based on latency budget, customer tier, and recent anomaly score.

For 'medium' and 'high' buckets we store a compact snapshot per decision containing: routing policy input, chosen route(s), per-hop latency/cost micro-metrics, cache hits, and active fallback variant metadata.
Snapshots are stored in the observability store with configurable TTL and indexed by request_id, route_id, region, and model_variant.
Dashboard panels exist to filter snapshot rate by region/tier/model variant and to replay a decision trace for RCA without exposing raw PII.
End-to-end impact on p99 latency for normal requests is < 1% and additional cost is within budget for runtime-1.23 rollout.
Privacy review completed: snapshots are redacted for user content and hashed IDs.
Automated sampling can be toggled per-region and per-customer tier via feature flags for gradual rollout.
design_notes: We will not capture full token streams. Snapshots are intentionally compact: top-level routing input (first 256 bytes of prompt, hashed user id), a per-hop summary (hop index, node id, region, observed latency ms, estimated cost units, cache hit boolean), and the decision DAG with chosen fallback variant and rationale tag. Use a hybrid approach: deterministic bucketing for high confidence errors (e.g., invoked fallback) and probabilistic sampling otherwise. Sampling weights are adjusted by cost-estimate and customer_tier to prioritize visibility where it matters.
sampling_algorithm: 1) Compute base score = anomaly_score + (is_fallback ? 1.2 : 0) + (customer_tier == 'enterprise' ? 0.5 : 0). 2) Estimate marginal cost units for snapshot. 3) Map score/cost to bucket: score>1.5=>high, 0.8-1.5=>medium, 0.2-0.8=>low, else none. 4) Apply reservoir sampling per-second window per-region to cap high-bucket rate. 5) Respect customer opt-out and privacy flags.
storage_plan: Snapshots are routed to the observability topic 'routing-snapshots' and stored in our hot index for 7 days, then cold archived to S3 for 90 days for support investigations. High-bucket samples are retained in hot index for 30 days. Each snapshot is compressed with snappy and limited to 64KB after redaction. Indexed fields: request_id, timestamp, region, cluster_tier, model_variant, route_policy_id.
retention_policy: none,low: 7 days hot; medium: 30 days hot; high: 30 days hot + 90 days cold archive
observability_queries: Panels: snapshot-rate-by-region-tier -> group by region, cluster_tier, bucket
Query: failures-with-fallback -> filter where snapshot.decision.used_fallback == true | count by model_variant, region
Trace viewer: reconstruct per-hop timeline from snapshot.per_hop[*] and overlay model_variant latency distributions
Cost panel: estimated-snapshot-cost -> sum(snapshot.estimated_cost_units) by day, region

risks: Snapshot size could exceed the 64KB limit for long prompts if redaction fails; mitigated by server-side truncation and tests.
Incorrect bucketing could bias visibility away from lower-tier customers causing missed regressions; mitigate with periodic audits and synthetic traffic targeting low tiers.
Ingest pipeline could increase load on observability cluster during bursts; reservoir caps and backpressure fallback (drop to low/none) defined.
Privacy exposure if hashing is reversible; we will use HMAC with a rotating key and store only hashed IDs in snapshots.
